1: Log4Qt - Logging for the Qt cross-platform application framework
2: ================================================================
3: 
4: Continuous Integration
5: ----------------------
6: [![CMake Ubuntu build and test](https://github.com/MEONMedical/Log4Qt/actions/workflows/cmake-ubuntu.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MEONMedical/Log4Qt/actions/workflows/cmake-ubuntu.yml)

11: Description
12: -----------
13: Log4Qt is a C++ port of the Apache Software Foundation Log4j package using the Qt Framework.
14: It is intended to be used by open source and commercial Qt projects.
15: 
16: Original project
17: ----------------
18: http://log4qt.sourceforge.net/
19: 
20: This Log4Qt repository is a clone of the Log4Qt repository from https://gitorious.org/log4qt
21: which was itself a clone of the original Log4Qt project on SourceForge http://sourceforge.net/projects/log4qt/ (http://log4qt.sourceforge.net/).
22: 
23: Additional features
24: -------------------
25: * JSON configuration support (`log4qt.json`) alongside the classic `.properties` format
26: * XML configuration support (`log4qt.xml`) alongside `.properties` and `.json` formats
27: * Pluggable TriggeringPolicy / RolloverStrategy for RollingFileAppender (log4j2-style):
28:   size-based, time-based, cron-based, and on-startup triggering policies with
29:   composable OR-combination and a fixed-window numbered rollover strategy
30: * SimpleTimeLayout (“dd.MM.yyyy hh:mm [Thread] Level Logger Message”)
31: * ColorConsoleAppender (render colorized message by escape sequence and put it to console)
32: * SignalAppender (emit signal when log event happens)
33: * DatabaseAppender (append log event into sql table)
34: * DatabaseLayout (put log event into sql table columns)
35: * Telnet appender (append log event to telnet clients)
36: * LogStream (qDebug()-style log messages appending)
37: * MainThreadAppender (Proxy appender for sending log messages through event loop)
38: * XMLLayout to support apache chainsaw
39: * DailyRollingFileAppender which generates a logfile for each day (add current date formatted to the filename)
40: * Binary logger
41: * Windows Debug Console Appender
42: 
43: JSON Configuration
44: ------------------
45: As an alternative to `log4qt.properties`, you can use a `log4qt.json` file:
46: 
47: ```json
48: {
49:     "log4j": {
50:         "rootLogger": "DEBUG, console",
51:         "appender": {
52:             "console": {
53:                 "type": "org.apache.log4j.ConsoleAppender",
54:                 "target": "STDOUT_TARGET",
55:                 "layout": {
56:                     "type": "org.apache.log4j.TTCCLayout",
57:                     "dateFormat": "ISO8601"
58:                 }
59:             }
60:         },
61:         "logger": {
62:             "MyApp": "ERROR, console"
63:         },
64:         "additivity": {
65:             "MyApp": "false"
66:         }
67:     }
68: }
69: ```
70: 
71: Nested objects produce dot-separated property keys, and the `type` key sets the class
72: (appender, layout, filter, …) for the parent object — **not** `class` or `@class`. The
73: value accepts the legacy `org.apache.log4j.*` names, the `Log4Qt::*` names, or the short
74: aliases (e.g. `Console`, `TTCCLayout`). Place the file next to your executable or in the
75: working directory. When both `log4qt.properties` and `log4qt.json` exist, the `.properties`
76: file takes priority.
77: 
78: You can also configure programmatically:
79: 
80: ```cpp
81: #include <log4qt/jsonconfigurator.h>
82: 
83: Log4Qt::JsonConfigurator::configure("path/to/config.json");
84: // or with file watching:
85: Log4Qt::JsonConfigurator::configureAndWatch("path/to/config.json");
86: ```
87: 
88: XML Configuration
89: ------------------
90: As an alternative to `.properties` and `.json`, you can use a `log4qt.xml` file:
91: 
92: ```xml
93: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
94: <log4j>
95:     <rootLogger>DEBUG, console</rootLogger>
96:     <appender>
97:         <console>
98:             <type>org.apache.log4j.ConsoleAppender</type>
99:             <target>STDOUT_TARGET</target>
100:             <layout>
101:                 <type>org.apache.log4j.TTCCLayout</type>
102:                 <dateFormat>ISO8601</dateFormat>
103:             </layout>
104:         </console>
105:     </appender>
106:     <logger>
107:         <MyApp>ERROR, console</MyApp>
108:     </logger>
109:     <additivity>
110:         <MyApp>false</MyApp>
111:     </additivity>
112: </log4j>
113: ```
114: 
115: Nested elements produce dot-separated property keys, and a `<type>` element sets the class
116: for the parent element — **not** a `class` attribute as in Log4j's XML. (Attributes flatten
117: to child properties, so `type="..."` as an attribute also works, but `class="..."` does
118: not.) Priority order: `.properties` > `.json` > `.xml`.
119: 
120: You can also configure programmatically:
121: 
122: ```cpp
123: #include <log4qt/xmlconfigurator.h>
124: 
125: Log4Qt::XmlConfigurator::configure("path/to/config.xml");
126: // or with file watching:
127: Log4Qt::XmlConfigurator::configureAndWatch("path/to/config.xml");
128: ```
129: 
130: Requirements
131: ------------
132: * Minimum Qt version required Qt 6.4 (for support of Qt versions down to 5.3 use branch 1.4 or the lates 1.4.x release
133:   or for support of Qt versions down to 5.7 use branch 1.6 or the lates 1.5.x release)
134: * C++20 required (minimum compiler version MSVC 19.29 (Visual Studio 2019 16.11), GCC 10, or Clang 10)
